text:
incident-bot: ALERT: GPU pool `us-west-2-prod-gpu` at 100% utilization. queue_depth=12,400 reqs (+320% over 5m). autoscaler failed to scale beyond 80 GPUs (error: "scale limit reached"). Impact: increased latency and 503 throttles for some customer traffic. Paging on-call infra.
sam: Oncall here — acknowledging. I’m grabbing context and will coordinate mitigations. tagging @maria @alex @jess. :eyes:
maria: joining. pulling autoscaler logs and k8s events now. first glance — controller saw provisioning errors from cloud provider: "quota_exceeded: GPUsPerProjectLimit". will paste logs.
alex: I see provider quota error in the cloud console too: project quota for GPUs = 80, usage=80. No further nodes can be created until quota is increased or existing VMs freed. Also seeing a few failed instance creates: `vm quota CPU limit` warnings intermittently.
jess: Runtime note — several high-RPS customers are pinned to the large-56g model variant which is causing long-run GPU occupancy per request. We can fallback those routes to 7b-quantized variants temporarily to reduce per-request GPU time.
sam: Mitigation plan (short): 1) Temporary emergency scaling path: bring up pre-warmed "burst" pool from dedicated reserve in us-west-2. 2) Evict/abort low-priority batch jobs and dequeue non-urgent workloads. 3) Re-route PLG traffic to smaller quantized variants. 4) Request quota increase from cloud. Who can execute 1 & 2 now?
ops-eng: I can run the pool activation. Command to open the burst pool:

```
# create emergency burst pool (pre-provisioned nodes template)
redwoodctl pools activate --name us-west-2-burst --size 40 --template prod-gpu-v2
```

I’ll kick that off now and watch node joins.
maria: Starting batch eviction script. Running:

```
/opt/redwood/sbin/evict_low_priority.sh --pool us-west-2-prod-gpu --age 300 --threshold 100
```

This will abort queued background requests and mark them for client retry. Posting logs:

```
[2026-03-15T19:42:17Z] evict: found 142 low-priority jobs -> aborting
[2026-03-15T19:42:20Z] evict: freed ~9 GPUs worth of capacity
```

maria: eviction complete — reclaimed ~9 GPU-equivalents. queue_depth -> 10,800.
ops-eng: burst pool request submitted. deploy-bot: "pool activation started". kube nodes appearing, kubelet registering... now 24/40 nodes ready.
deploy-bot: pool us-west-2-burst activation progress: 60% (24/40 nodes ready).
alex: I’ve opened a quota request with cloud support (ticket CLOUD-7331) asking for GPUs -> 200 for the project. ETA unknown but I flagged as P0.
cs-rep: Notifying affected customers. Currently 3 customers reported increased errors: acct-PLG-112, acct-enterprise-44, acct-startup-901. Sending interim status message: we are mitigating, partial degradation. Will update once queue < 2k.
sam: Also enabling runtime fallback policy for non-critical routes. Jess — can you patch traffic rules to send model variants for /v1/generate? Example rule change:

```
routes:
  - path: /v1/generate
    when: traffic_tier == "plg"
    model_override: "7b-quantized"
```

jess: Done. Pushed canary to 10% first, checking latency & errors. No obvious regressions.
ops-eng: pool ready: 40/40 nodes. autoscaler sees capacity, starting to schedule pending pods. queue depth 6,100 and falling.
sam: Good. Are we still seeing autoscaler backoff errors or is it resolved now that the burst pool is active?
maria: autoscaler logs show successful node additions after pool came up. The original "scale limit reached" error persists in historical logs but new attempts are succeeding. We still need the cloud quota increase permanent fix.
alex: Cloud support replied — provisional increase approved to 150 while they review for 200. They applied it. We can rely on that for now. Ticket CLOUD-7331 updated.
cs-rep: Customers updated. One enterprise customer asked for an RCA and SLA credit if they suffered replays — flagged to SRE and CS leadership.
sam: Final status: queue back to 800, tail latency normalized. No major data loss; some client requests were aborted by eviction script (we logged request ids and will provide retry guidance). Marking incident as mitigated.
jenkins-bot: deploy log: "route-change canary -> 10% applied" :white_check_mark:
ops-eng: creating follow-up runbook PR for emergency burst pool activation and a checklist for when GPU quota is exhausted.
maria: Action items (captured):
- ACTION-1: Increase default cloud GPU quota to 200 and monitor for 7 days (owner: alex)
- ACTION-2: Add alert for queue_depth > 2k sustained over 3m (owner: sam)
- ACTION-3: Create runbook for emergency burst pool activation + automation to toggle routing fallbacks (owner: ops-eng)
- ACTION-4: Add autoscaler metric for "scale_failure_reason" to SLO dashboards (owner: maria)
- ACTION-5: CS to prepare customer-facing RCA template (owner: cs-rep)

sam: I’m handing off post-incident follow-up to @maria for next 24h and switching out of pager. Thanks everyone who jumped in. :heart:
maria: Taking handoff. Will kick off postmortem doc and link to this thread. Expect initial draft in 24h.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status=mitigated, severity=high, start_ts=1912345678, mitigated_ts=1912345702, incident_id=INC-2026-0315-01. Postmortem required. :page_with_curl:
alex: noted. filing infra ticket INFRA-498 to automate quota prechecks and pre-warm burst pool when usage > 70%.
sam: closing channel for active mitigations. If any regression occurs, reopen and page SRE. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
